summary: Mexico's new electricity laws reserve at least 54% of dispatched power for the state utility CFE, and private utility-scale projects must sell to CFE. Profits can be repatriated freely, but the policy shift and unclear regulation weigh on private renewables.

access.reason: Private utility-scale projects now sell exclusively to CFE, which must supply at least 54% of power dispatched to the grid.

ownership.reason: There are no controls on transferring US dollars, and profits can be repatriated freely.

build.reason: Larger projects face unclear regulation and paralysis at the energy authorities, and new transmission is needed.

stability.reason: New laws reversed the earlier open market by guaranteeing CFE a majority share of generation.

direction.reason: Plan México gives CFE most of the 2030 capacity build, with private investment limited to about 6.4 GW.

access.reason: Self-generation of 0.7 to 20 MW can connect to the grid, but surplus power must be sold only to CFE.

build.reason: Smaller projects benefit from a fast-track interconnection process.

stability.reason: The new laws favour CFE, though self-generation remains allowed.

direction.reason: Self-generation rules were set out in the new laws.

events.title: New electricity laws require at least 54% of dispatched power to come from CFE

gaps: Contract terms with CFE, buyer credit and the status of earlier private contracts were not covered by the sources reviewed.
